newsitem.title: RWANDA: Third Rwandan genocide suspect sentenced to death.
newsitem.headline: Third Rwandan genocide suspect sentenced to death.

text.p: A court in the northwestern Rwandan town of Byumba has sentenced to death a third suspect charged with participation in the 1994 genocide in which 800,000 ethnic Tutsis and moderate Hutus were slaughtered.
"Francois Bizimutima was sentenced yesterday (Friday), he received the death penalty. He will be able to appeal," a justice ministry official told Reuters.
Under Rwanda's law, the accused has 15 days to appeal and the appeals court must hand down judgment in three months.
Bizimutima is the third suspect to be sentenced to death -- by firing squad under Rwandan law. Rwanda's genocide trials began on December 27 and some 37 are scheduled to be tried.
Bizimutima was a former secondary school teacher in Rutare commune. He was also a former chairman of the Coalition for the Defence of the Republic CDR in the same commune.
He appeared before the court on January 10, charged principally with organizing and perpetrating genocide and massacres and setting up a criminal group.
